components.basis: Definition with partition representation, finite nonnegative coefficients, extended-arithmetic conventions (0*inf=0) and representation independence (proved in the C002 annex item). The source variant (Durrett p. 18: sigma-finite measure, simple functions on finite-measure pieces) is identified at body 11-16 and bridged by the proved comparison thm:p15-integral-source-bridge.

Well-definedness, additivity, scaling including the zero scalar, monotonicity, the indicator formula and the overlapping-sets formula are stated and proved by common refinement, including infinite measures.
Supremum definition, nonemptiness, value range, restricted integral including infinite values, the a.e. definition and the measurable-replacement/no-completeness stipulation are all present.

Agreement with the simple integral, monotonicity and monotone convergence proved directly (theta-scaling argument) including the infinite cases; the nonnegativity boundary is worked by r_n in C011. Durrett derives MCT from Fatou (Thm 1.5.7, p. 27); the handbook route is stated at body 13-15.
Additivity, scaling, the series formula, the zero-integral criterion in both directions, finiteness a.e., a.e. order and invariance, a.e. MCT, Fatou and the measure nu_f are all proved.

Parts, signed integral with its existence condition, the undefined case not assigned by cancellation, integrability, restricted integral and finite representative; measurability of the parts is proved in the annex and the undefined case is worked in C018.
Linearity, absolute bound, a.e. order, a.e. replacement, difference formula and countable additivity with absolute convergence (Durrett Ex. 1.5.4 and 1.6.16 content) are proved.
The bounded finite-support sup/inf identity and the sigma-finite truncation identity are proved, with the explicit identification with Durrett's four stages (source pp. 18-22).

p-sizes, the essential bound with the empty-infimum convention, L^1 classes with the norm facts (proved at annex 184-188), L^1 convergence and convergence in measure/probability are defined; no completeness is claimed.

Dominated convergence in L^1 via Fatou with null-set reductions; bounded convergence in measure (Durrett Thm 1.5.3, p. 26) including derivation of the limit bounds; the uniformly bounded a.e. case (Durrett Thm 1.6.7 special case) is proved.

Strict Fatou example with the no-dominator computation and harmonic divergence argument, signed Fatou failure, infinite-domain failure of bounded convergence (Durrett Ex. 1.5.4) and failure of MCT without nonnegativity are worked inline.
All p,q in [1,inf] including zero/infinite-norm cases; Young's inequality proved; endpoint cases; Cauchy-Schwarz. Covers both source forms (Thm 1.5.2 with (1,inf), Thm 1.6.3 with [1,inf]).
Definition; the promised continuity and supporting affine function at every real point are proved in the annex.
Measurability of phi(f), supporting line without differentiability, integration under the stated normalization and integrability hypotheses (Durrett Thm 1.5.1 / 1.6.2).

Expectation with existence conventions (Durrett p. 28), finite mean, restricted expectation, k-th moment and variance; the promised justification (finite mean from a finite second moment) is at annex 477-481.

Inherited laws, the affine formula including infinite-expectation branches, integration over the law by indicator/simple/nonnegative/signed steps (Durrett Thm 1.6.9), integrability on either space and the atomic sum with absolute convergence are proved.

General nonnegative-function bound (Durrett Thm 1.6.4) including empty A, Markov, integrability from the second moment, the variance identity, affine variance and the Chebyshev variance bound are proved; the source naming variant is recorded at body 373-375.

Uniform mean, second moment and variance by simple bounds; the summation identities, the bounds and the limits are proved at the cited routed w02b-p15-001 theorem; the undefined signed mean example computes the total mass and both infinite part expectations inline.
Durrett Thm 1.6.8 (p. 31) with integrability of h(X_n) and h(X), choice of M with P(|X|=M)=0, truncation, bounded convergence, the error bound and the p-th moment example are proved.

Proof boundary: its claim that every theorem of the chapter has a complete annex proof holds (each hbtheorem carries a proved= annex item, all present), and each pointer resolves on the current route to theorems with declared annex proofs: interval/step/continuous approximation and Riemann-Lebesgue (Ex. 1.4.3-1.4.4), dyadic, truncation, small-set and simple approximations (Ex. 1.4.2, 1.5.7, 1.5.9), essential bound, norm limit, Minkowski and L^p (Ex. 1.5.1-1.5.3), Poisson and geometric moments (Examples 1.6.13-1.6.14), density representation, conditional calculus, L^p contraction, L^2 projection, product measures and Fubini, and the exponential, gamma and normal calculations (Examples 1.6.10-1.6.11).
